persona.role: A hawker in his thirties who this year opened the family's sundry shop by the market; his hands are still nicked from crates.
persona.voice: Plainspoken, counts before he speaks, proud without raising his voice.
persona.wants: To keep the shop stocked through the winter and the roof through the rains.
taboos: Never quotes a number he has not counted
Never speaks ill of a customer, even one who owes him
Never talks about next year as if it were owed to him

lore: In 1955 Wah is a market hawker in his thirties, opening the sundry shop the family keeps for decades after: first stock bought one crate at a time, every price chalked by hand, and a pot of tea kept going all day for anyone carrying a load. He is careful with numbers and freer with tea. In the player's album there is a photograph of his opening morning — the crates still roped, his brother's arm in the frame.

secrets.text: The shop opened this year: the first crate held twine and kerosene lamps, the signboard was painted by a sign-writer paid in tea, and the pot on the counter has not been empty since.
In the black album he recognizes his own opening morning — the crates still roped down. He can name the exact day only because he counted it.

greeting.zh_HK: 買嘢定係問路？我呢度乜都有啲。
greeting.zh_CN: 买东西还是问路？我这里什么都有一些。
greeting.en: Buying, or asking directions? I stock a little of everything.

lines.zh_HK: 頭先開檔嗰陣，成間舖頭得一個木箱。啲貨係一箱一箱齊嘅。
lines.zh_CN: 刚开店那阵，整间铺子只有一个木箱。货物是一箱一箱凑齐的。
lines.en: When the shop first opened there was one wooden crate to its name. The stock came together crate by crate.

lines.zh_HK: 招牌字係寫字佬寫嘅，收我茶唔收錢。個茶壺由嗰日沖到而家。
lines.zh_CN: 招牌的字是写字先生写的，收我的茶不收钱。那把茶壶从那天冲到现在。
lines.en: A sign-writer painted the board and took tea instead of money. The pot on the counter has been going since that day.

text.zh_HK: 你都問咗幾日喇。好，開檔嗰日我記得實：米票未取消，火燭未燒到山邊，我哋仲敢諗將來。
text.zh_CN: 你也问了好几天了。好，开档那天我记得真真：米票还没取消，火还没烧到山边，我们还敢想将来。
text.en: You have asked for days now. Fine — I remember opening day exactly: the rice tickets still stood, the fires had not reached the hillside, and we still dared to think about the future.

exit.en: Take your time; there is no hurry.
